For each user, record paired binary hits on identical pinned candidates: dᵤ = hit_B@10 − hit_A@10. The category difference is mean(dᵤ); the benchmark difference is the equally weighted mean across four categories. Recommended category-stratified paired bootstrap: independently resample 200 users with replacement within each category, preserve both models’ outcomes together, recompute the macro difference, and report the 2.5th–97.5th percentiles over, for example, 10,000 replicates. Keep candidates fixed; do not resample negatives or treat candidate items as independent observations. Report percentage-point differences, category results, and discordant counts—B-only hits versus A-only hits. This applies the [paired-bootstrap principle documented by SciPy](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html) to the pinned macro metric.

Selecting the best checkpoint and repeatedly adapting proposals against the same validation users creates selection optimism. Disclose checkpoint-selection rules, evaluation frequency, checkpoints/proposals examined, and adaptive validation reuse. Label resulting intervals exploratory and conditional on the selected models: bootstrapping their fixed predictions does not correct the selection process. Reserve confirmatory claims for the host’s untouched final evaluation; leave the evaluator unchanged. [Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html) show that optimizing finite-sample selection criteria can materially bias reported performance.

These intervals estimate user-sampling uncertainty within the four fixed categories, conditional on trained weights, splits, and sampled candidates; the observed benchmark score itself is fixed. They exclude training-seed variability, candidate-resampling variability, and uncertainty across other categories. With training seed 42 only, report training-seed uncertainty as unmeasured; bootstrap replicates are not independent training runs. [Bouthillier et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03098) distinguish data-sampling, initialization, and hyperparameter sources of benchmark variation.
